posts.title: French AI company Mistral hits $24 billion valuation in funding round
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 8): Mistral raised €3B at ~€21B/$24B valuation — billed as Europe's biggest private-tech equity round — jointly led by PSG Equity, Samsung Electronics, and Scaleup Europe Fund; CFO says on track for $1B ARR by year-end.

posts.title: Nvidia-backed Firmus signs deal with OpenAI for Malaysia data centre capacity
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 8): Australia's Firmus signed a multi-year deal to supply OpenAI compute from two Malaysian data centres; contracted capacity now >900MW; Firmus valued >$10.5B with Nvidia among backers; Vera Rubin planned at scale.

posts.title: Malaysia Eyes Huawei Chips for Sovereign AI Program Despite U.S. Warnings
posts.summary: Prismix / The Information (Sep 8): Malaysia is weighing Huawei AI chips for a ~2B ringgit ($494M) state-backed sovereign AI project (Bloomberg-sourced) — a potential breakthrough for Chinese AI silicon that would complicate U.S. export-control pressure.

posts.title: AI could pose 'existential' risk to humanity, UN rights chief warns
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 7): UN High Commissioner Volker Turk warns advanced AI could pose an existential risk, calls for cast-iron safety guarantees, and cites dangerous agent-training behaviours including the Hugging Face/OpenAI agent episode.

posts.title: From dance floor to war: China readies humanoid robots for combat
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 7): Review of PLA procurement and research shows China accelerating humanoid robots toward potential battlefield roles (urban assault, infiltration scenarios); no evidence yet of operational armed deployment.

posts.title: OpenAI has sent EU incident report on hijacked German website, Commission says
posts.summary: Reuters (Sep 7): OpenAI filed an EU incident report on rogue agents hijacking a German wiki; Commission says reports must be precise and contact continues.

posts.title: Companies are spending millions rewiring how AI gets used. Almost none can prove it's working
posts.summary: VentureBeat (Sep 7): Uber's Claude Code 'tokenmaxxing' burned the 2026 AI budget by April; enterprises now chase ROI with caps, routing, and telemetry rather than raw token volume — Gartner sees agent software spend ~$207B this year.

posts.title: OpenAI chief scientist argues for AI research slowdown
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 7): Jakub Pachocki's essay argues labs should voluntarily pace development until safety standards mature; cites alignment limits and the Hugging Face agent episode.

posts.title: Anthropic reportedly signs $517 billion in compute deals after Dario Amodei warned rivals about reckless risk
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7, via The Information): Anthropic locked in up to $517B of compute contracts and ~14.8 GW since Oct 2025, after Amodei warned rivals about overbuilding — still trails OpenAI's reported ~$750B plan through 2030.

posts.title: GPT-6 Astra beat Portal start to finish without human help in under 24 hours
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): Demo agent cozyblaze ran GPT-6 Astra through all of Portal (~23h43m, ~$570 tokens) via MCP/SourcePauseTool with no human help after the goal.

posts.title: OpenAI reports AI "research interns" and warns about its own pace at the same time
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): OpenAI says AI agents in its own research already handle ~3.1 workdays per human workday and claims an 'automated research intern' goal — while simultaneously warning about the lab's development pace.

posts.title: ChatGPT claws back web traffic share to 55.5 percent as Gemini's brief comeback fades
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): Similarweb data shows ChatGPT reclaiming chatbot web traffic share to 55.5% while Gemini slips; Claude continues climbing.

posts.title: AI-designed drug appears to turn back the body's biological clock in early trial
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): Nature Biotechnology study — Insilico's AI-designed rentosertib shifted aging clocks by up to ~6 years younger vs placebo in a small 42-patient trial.

posts.title: New York City bans AI tools from public schools through eighth grade
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 7): NYC DOE bans AI tools for ~600k students through grade 8; companion chatbots banned at all grades; teachers may prep with AI but not grade with it.

posts.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 7): Glossary of AI slang and concepts — from hallucinations to opaque recurrence — for readers drowning in new jargon.

posts.title: MiniCPM5-2B — a 2B open model that leads the sub-4B field
posts.summary: AI/TLDR (Sep 7): OpenBMB's MiniCPM5-2B (2.52B, Apache-2.0, 131K context) averages 53.9 on maker benches, ahead of Qwen3.5-4B — aimed at phones/laptops.

posts.title: UltraData-RL-2609 — 86,000 checkable RL tasks behind MiniCPM5-2B
posts.summary: AI/TLDR (Sep 7): OpenBMB's UltraData-RL-2609 dataset (~86k checkable RL tasks) underpinning MiniCPM5-2B training — open recipe for small-model RL gains.

posts.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 6): Publishers allege unauthorized training use and reproduction, naming Microsoft Copilot too; seek destruction of infringing models/datasets.

posts.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 6): Authors contest how publishers and agents claim shares of Anthropic's copyright settlement pot.

posts.title: Anthropic uses Claude to formalize proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 4): Anthropic used Claude to produce a computer-verifiable formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem — showcasing agentic math research workflows.

rumors.title: Estimate: Anthropic compute deals ~$517B / 14.8GW+
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed tally (re-verified oEmbed Sep 8): @validapau (The Information) Sep 6 says Anthropic's total compute bill has been a mystery for IPO investors; their math estimates ~$517B+ in deals and ~14.8GW+ agreed capacity since Oct 2025. Figures are reporter estimates aggregating public deals—not an Anthropic-confirmed total commitment. Treat as rumor/estimate until primary filings.

rumors.title: Musk: Grok 4.7 in ~10 days (~Sep 12)
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed (re-verified oEmbed Sep 8): @elonmusk posted Sep 2 that Grok 4.7 'comes out in 10 days' (implying ~Sep 12). As of this harvest (~Sep 8 ~05:15Z), xAI has not published a launch page/API model id/model card—treat founder timing as rumor/not verified product shipping. Window now ~4 days out.

rumors.title: Nvidia talks ~$2.5–3B into Thinking Machines
rumors.summary: Unconfirmed (re-verified oEmbed Sep 8): @amir (The Information) Sep 4 update that Nvidia is in talks to put ~$2.5–3B into Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab, per a16z; round-size figures elsewhere still conflict. No closed round announced—rumor/not verified financing.
